challenges_to_claims.issue: The canary passing is a narrow detector sanity check, not evidence about real feature leakage or proxy behavior. It cannot support any conclusion about the dataset columns under audit.

The statement 'Declared decision-time exclusions for credit_default: none' is not justified as a decision. The package lacks decision-time semantics and production-availability review for actual columns, so 'none' is unsupported.

review.decision: Insufficient evidence to identify or clear any specific columns as contract-safe. No feature should be approved from this package alone.
review.interpretation: This package provides only a minimal audit signal: the detector can recognize an injected exact-target canary, but there is no evidence here that any real column was tested, ranked, or validated against decision-time availability. The empty declared leakage list is not sufficient to conclude absence of leakage or absence of target proxies, especially because the comparative safe_vs_unsafe_training_cv result is missing.

next_experiment.hypothesis: At least one column flagged by simple heuristics (name similarity to target, high univariate AUC, near-uniqueness, or post-outcome timing) will fail a decision-time availability review or show suspicious proxy behavior.
next_experiment.success_gate: For every column in the dataset, provide a decision-time availability label and a minimal evidence trace; any column with post-outcome timing, target-derived naming, or unusually strong univariate association must be explicitly reviewed and either justified as available at prediction time or marked excluded.
next_experiment.title: Column-level decision-time contract audit for candidate proxies
next_experiment.why_smallest: This is the smallest falsifiable step because it reuses the existing leakage-audit framing and adds only per-column metadata review plus a lightweight heuristic screen, without requiring model retraining or broader experimental redesign.
